records.sourceFile: Thriving on Pressure- A Factor Mixture Analysis of Sport Performers’ Responses to Competitive Encounters.pdf

paper.citation: Brown DJ, Arnold R, Standage M, Fletcher D. Thriving on Pressure: A Factor Mixture Analysis of Sport Performers' Responses to Competitive Encounters. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology. 2017;39(6):423-437.
paper.abstract: Factor mixture analysis of 535 sport performers' responses to demanding competitive encounters over the past month, using subjective performance, vitality and positive affect. Four profiles emerged, and resilient qualities, psychological skills, need satisfaction and frustration, and challenge appraisal predicted profile membership.
paper.tldr: Competitive athletes who thrived in demanding events rated both their performance and well-being highly, and this group could be identified statistically. Resilience, psychological skills, need satisfaction and challenge appraisal were linked to thriving, so these are candidate targets for practice.
paper.methods: Questionnaire on performance and well-being in demanding competitions over the past month. Measures included self-rated performance (0 to 10), subjective vitality, positive affect, resilient qualities, psychological skills use, social support, coach need-supportive and need-thwarting behavior, challenge and threat appraisal, and basic psychological needs. Factor mixture models with one to six profiles were compared on fit and interpretability.
paper.findings: Four profiles were retained: thriving (27.9%), above average (25.0%), below average (39.9%) and low functioning (7.3%). Higher resilient qualities lowered the odds of membership in each of the other three profiles relative to thriving, and greater psychological skills use lowered the odds of the below-average and low-functioning profiles. Higher need satisfaction lowered the odds of all three, higher need frustration raised the odds of the below-average profile, challenge appraisal lowered the odds of the low-functioning profile, and social support and coach behaviors did not predict membership.
paper.limitations: The analysis is data-driven and cross-sectional, and the authors call for replication. Subjective performance is a single self-rated item, and the thriving and above-average profiles may overlap on it. The sample is mostly male, mostly British and mostly at regional or senior level, with only 0.7% professional.
paper.practicalImplications: Practitioners who want to support thriving could work on resilient qualities, psychological skills, the satisfaction of autonomy, competence and relatedness needs, and how athletes appraise competition as a challenge. The authors suggest interventions that target both performance and well-being.
paper.athleteDev: Most of the sample were adult senior performers, although ages from 16 upward were included. The study offers a framework for thinking about resilience and psychological skills in athletes, but it does not test whether building these skills raises thriving over time.
paper.rtp: The study does not address injury, rehabilitation or return to sport, and its participants were excluded if injury kept them from competing. It cannot be used to judge readiness to return after injury or to predict re-injury.
